newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end down after U.S. stocks rebound.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end down after U.S. stocks rebound.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mostly lower on profit-taking, as the U.S. stock market's firm tone supported the dollar, traders and anlaysts said.
"The dollar is going wherever the stock market is going," one currency analyst said. "Friday's sell-off is what got people fixated on stocks."

September marks fell through support at $0.5444, or 1.8400 spot marks, as the U.S. stock market continued to rebound from Monday's session. September nudged below $0.5436 or 1.8427 spot marks, as U.S. stocks managed to sustain their rally around midday, they said.
September Swiss francs also fell near a key support level of $0.6607 or 1.5181 spot.
He said some traders, lulled by the dollar's range bound activity, may be surprised if the Bundesbank were to change German monetary policy at Thursday's meeting.
"Since everyone has stopped looking at German rates, there is now a higher potential for the Bundesbank to do something," he said. "They could go to a variable repo for shock value."
He said a shift to a variable repo from a fixed repo rate would lift September marks to $0.5565, or 1.80 spot, above the 3-1/2-week high of $0.5548 set on Monday.

The rebound in the U.S. stock market, coupled with the Bundesbank's decision to leave the repo at a three-percent fixed rate at Tuesday's weekly tender, dampened speculation about higher German interest rates, they said.
September yen gravitated above the upper end of its recent range, but remained lower throughout the day.
Some traders said the selling of Southeast Asian currencies weighed on yen, instead of providing the currency with a safe-haven status.
The Indonesian rupiah dropped through a key support level overnight, which weighed on the Singapore dollar.
The weakness in the region's currencies could drag down the Hong Kong dollar, they said.
"I don't think Japan is benefiting from any this," another analyst said. "It's bad for the region's economy, and if anything you are seeing a funds flow to Australian dollars."
Australian dollar futures and Mexican pesos were the only currencies able to hold gains on Tuesday.

Overall the market had little reaction to the Federal Open Market Committee's decision to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged. Traders are now focusing on the U.S. June international trade data on Wednesday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.
The U.S. trade deficit is forecast to widen to $10.36 billion from $10.23 billion in May.

At the end of pit trade, September yen was off $0.000025 at $0.008494, marks were down $0.0035 at $0.5449, Swiss francs were $0.0012 lower at $0.6624, sterling was $0.0058 lower at $1.6034, Canadian dollars were off $0.0032 at $0.7183, Australian dollars were $0.0031 higher at $0.7417 and Mexican pesos rose $0.000125 at $0.127350. (Chicago Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750))
